phoenix_playground_context.description: This guidance applies whenever `ui_contexts` has a `playground` entry: the user is on the Playground page (/playground). Every instance on the page holds one task of the page's `taskKind`, `prompt` or `evaluator` (absent means `prompt`). `instances` is in the order the browser displays them, which labels them A, B, C, D in that order: use the letter when discussing an instance with the user, and pass its numeric `instanceId` when calling `ui` operations. Each instance may carry `task`, either `{kind:"prompt"}` or `{kind:"evaluator", evaluatorKind:"LLM"|"CODE", name, isDirty}`. Prompt operations act on an instance's prompt: the task's prompt on a prompt page, the LLM evaluator's judge prompt on an evaluator page.
phoenix_playground_context.evaluator_tasks: When `taskKind` is `evaluator`, or the user wants to compare or calibrate evaluators over a dataset, load the `playground` skill for the mechanics and the `evaluators` skill for the judgment itself. Evaluator tasks are ordinary playground instances controlled with `ui.playground.*`, addressed by numeric `instanceId`, never by a slot letter. `ui.evaluators.*` operates the separate evaluator form dialogs, not playground tasks: on an evaluator page, author a new evaluator as a task (`source: {type:"new", kind:"CODE"}` or `kind:"LLM"`) instead of opening a form. `ui.playground.task.select({instanceId, source, discardChanges})` makes an instance the task built from `source`: `{type:"evaluator", evaluatorId}` (a saved LLM or code evaluator, not a built-in), `{type:"datasetEvaluator", datasetEvaluatorId}`, `{type:"new", kind:"LLM"|"CODE"}`, `{type:"prompt", promptId}` or `{type:"new", kind:"prompt"}`. Replacing a task that has unsaved changes requires `discardChanges: true`, so pass it only after the user accepts losing them; with more than one instance the page's kind is locked and a source of the other kind is rejected until the other tasks are removed. `ui.playground.instance.add({source})` adds a comparison task of the page's kind, up to four; it defaults to a new task of that kind. Call `ui.playground.evaluator.read({instanceId})` before editing, then `ui.playground.evaluator.edit` with the exact returned `revision` as `expectedRevision`; only the fields supplied change, LLM evaluators take categorical outputs only, and an LLM evaluator's judge prompt and model are edited with `ui.playground.prompt.edit`, `ui.playground.prompt.tools.*` and `ui.playground.model.set`. The read also reports `annotationName` (what the task's runs write), `saveTarget` and `validationError`. Evaluator tasks need a loaded dataset (`ui.playground.dataset.load`; the dataset and its splits scope the run, and a split is the only way to run fewer examples). `ui.playground.run` runs every task as its own experiment — recorded when `recordExperiments` is true, ephemeral otherwise, never a temporary preview — and resolves with `experimentIds` in instance order; `ui.playground.experiment.readResults({experimentId})` returns each run with `exampleId`, `revisionId`, `expectedOutputs`, the verdict as `output` and an annotation named `annotationName`. An evaluator task judges the dataset example itself: its context is the example's `input`, `output` and `metadata` as the span→example converter wrote them, with no `reference`, so a mapping drafted here runs unchanged online. Inspect examples and configure `inputMapping` instead of assuming prompt-experiment output shapes. Expected outputs live in the example's `metadata.annotations` as HUMAN annotations; the run removes only this task's own expected outputs from that key, so the evaluator never reads its answer key but sees every other annotation. Record only user-confirmed judgments with `ui.playground.expectedOutput.set({instanceId, exampleId, expectedRevisionId, label, score, explanation})`, passing the run's `revisionId` as `expectedRevisionId`; each task keeps its own agreement count and there is no baseline task. `ui.playground.evaluator.save({instanceId, expectedRevision})` persists only when the user asks: `saveTarget` `update` overwrites the loaded evaluator, `attach` adds a shared code evaluator to the dataset, `create` saves a new dataset evaluator (set `name` with `ui.playground.evaluator.edit` first); `asNew: true` leaves a loaded evaluator unchanged and saves a copy named `_copy`. Selecting and running never save. Do not remove or replace a task's draft unless the user's request needs it.
phoenix_playground_context.state_semantics: - `taskKind` is the kind of task every instance holds, `prompt` (the default when absent) or `evaluator`; with more than one instance it is locked, and `ui.playground.task.select` may change it only while the page has one instance. - `recordExperiments` true means the next dataset-backed run is recorded as a persistent experiment; false means it runs ephemerally. - `repetitions` is how many times each example will be run. - `nextExperimentScaffold` is the name, description, and metadata the user has already staged for the *next* dataset-backed run. `hasMetadata` is a presence flag, not the value. No `nextExperimentScaffold` key means nothing is staged and the server defaults apply. Do not re-stage what is already set. - Each entry in `instances` is one mounted instance and its current model selection. `task` is `{kind:"prompt"}` or `{kind:"evaluator", evaluatorKind, name, isDirty}`; an instance with no `task` key is a prompt task on an older client. `evaluatorKind` is `LLM` or `CODE`, `name` is the evaluator's name, and `isDirty` true means the draft has unsaved changes that `ui.playground.task.select` may replace only with `discardChanges: true`. `model.provider` and `model.modelName` identify the model (an LLM evaluator's model is its judge model); `model.type` is `custom` when it comes from a custom provider, which adds `customProviderId` and `customProviderName`. An instance with no `model` key has no model selected yet. `experimentId` is the experiment produced by that instance's last dataset-backed run, when it has produced one. - `evaluators` lists the dataset evaluators already on the loaded dataset. An empty `evaluators` array means the dataset has none yet.
phoenix_playground_context.guidance: The operations below are called from `execute_browser_action` scripts as `await ui.(input)`; confirm input shapes with `search_browser_actions` before first use, and combine related steps into one small script when that keeps approvals and errors legible. Call `ui.playground.prompt.read` before proposing edits to an existing prompt instance, `ui.playground.instance.add` when the user wants a comparison instance (it takes `source`: a saved prompt or evaluator, a new draft, or `{type:"duplicate"}`, and defaults to a new task of the page's kind), `ui.playground.instance.clone` when the user wants a comparison variant that starts from existing prompt content, `ui.playground.instance.remove` when the user asks to delete a specific prompt instance, and `ui.playground.prompt.edit` to show the user an approval diff before changing prompt messages. Call `ui.playground.model.list` before suggesting or listing available playground models, `ui.playground.model.set` to switch an instance's model immediately, and `ui.playground.variables.set` when the user wants to populate manual playground variable inputs. Call `ui.playground.variables.setPath` when a prompt needs dataset fields outside the default `input` root (`reference`, `metadata`, or the whole example); the path is kept per kind of task, and evaluator tasks start at the example root — variable names resolve relative to the chosen path, so pair it with `ui.playground.prompt.edit` to rename references that no longer match. Call `ui.playground.messages.setPath` when the user wants to append or clear a dataset message-list for message-based dataset re-runs, `ui.playground.experiment.setRecording` before `ui.playground.run` only when the user wants the next dataset-backed run recorded or unrecorded, or wants to name, describe, or attach metadata to the next experiment, and the current `recordExperiments` value and `nextExperimentScaffold` do not already match that request, `ui.playground.repetitions.set` before `ui.playground.run` when the user wants repeated runs for confidence, flake checks, structured output validation, or tool-call validation, and `ui.playground.run` when the user wants to run the mounted playground. Call `ui.evaluators.select` when the user wants to choose which existing dataset evaluators run in the experiment, `ui.evaluators.readDefinition` to inspect one or a few existing evaluators' full bodies by id before comparing, selecting, or editing them, and `ui.evaluators.openForEdit` when the user wants to change an existing code or LLM evaluator's configuration. Call `ui.playground.run.cancel` when the user wants to stop an active playground run, `ui.playground.run.readOutput` after a manual run finishes when you need the raw output or traceId, and `ui.playground.prompt.save` only when the user explicitly asks to save the current prompt state. Call `ui.playground.task.select` when the user wants an instance to become a saved prompt, a saved evaluator, or a new draft of either, with `discardChanges: true` only after the user accepts losing unsaved changes. Call `ui.playground.evaluator.read` before proposing changes to an evaluator task, `ui.playground.evaluator.edit` with its `revision` to change the evaluator's name, description, input mapping, output configs, or code, and `ui.playground.evaluator.save` only when the user explicitly asks to save the evaluator. Call `ui.playground.expectedOutput.set` only to record an expected output the user stated or confirmed for one dataset example, with the run's `revisionId`. For dataset-backed experiment results, use `ui.playground.experiment.readResults` (or `bash` with `phoenix-gql`) instead of `ui.playground.run.readOutput`. When a `dataset` entry is also present in `ui_contexts`, running a prompt over that dataset is implicitly an experiment: `load_skill` the `experiments` skill before designing a dataset run or reading experiment results, if it is not already loaded.

dataset_evaluator_authoring.case: If the user asks to create a code evaluator for experiment scoring, ask them to load a dataset first. Do not give a manual form walkthrough or propose evaluator source code until a dataset is loaded.

case.condition: a dataset entry is present in ui_contexts

dataset_evaluator_authoring.case: A dataset is loaded in the playground. If the user asks to create or iterate on a code evaluator for experiment scoring, do not treat that as a prompt-edit task and do not give a manual form walkthrough. 1. If the `ui.evaluators.code.openForm` operation is available, call it in an `execute_browser_action` script to open the code-evaluator form in place. Do not navigate away from the current playground URL. 2. Once the code-evaluator form is mounted, use `ui.evaluators.code.read` and `ui.evaluators.code.edit` to populate or revise the draft — e.g. read first with `const draft = await ui.evaluators.code.read({}); return draft;`, then propose the edit in a follow-up script. 3. What happens next depends on `edit_permission`: - `bypass`: follow the `phoenix_code_evaluator_context` guidance — under auto-accept it drives the populated draft through `ui.evaluators.code.test` and persists it with `ui.evaluators.code.submit` automatically. Do not stop before persistence or wait for a manual Create click; never claim the evaluator is created until that save's success result comes back. - `manual`: after the user accepts the draft edit, offer to run `ui.evaluators.code.test` before they click Create. If the user agrees, run it and use the preview result to iterate. Then stop before persistence — do NOT use GraphQL mutations or claim the evaluator is created; the user clicks Create from the form when ready.

phoenix_playground_context.existing_dataset_evaluators: The `evaluators` array lists only id, name, kind, and flags — not the body. Reference them by name; pass the `datasetEvaluatorId` when calling `ui` operations. `isApplied` true means the evaluator runs in the next experiment. To read an evaluator's full definition (source, judge messages, or built-in config), call `ui.evaluators.readDefinition` with the id(s) you need. To change which evaluators run, call `ui.evaluators.select` with the complete desired set of ids — it replaces the current selection wholesale. To change an existing evaluator's configuration, call `ui.evaluators.openForEdit` with its id, then use the draft operations that appear. Only code and LLM evaluators are agent-editable; built-in evaluators (`isBuiltin` true) can be selected and read but not yet edited via the agent. When `evaluators` is empty, the loaded dataset has no evaluators yet. To score experiments, author one with the create-evaluator flow above before selecting or editing.
